entities.name: Marcus Papirius Mugillanus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Papirius Mugillanus was a prominent figure in the late Roman Republic, serving as consular tribune twice (418 and 416 BC) and possibly consul in 411 BC. 

As a key player in the Roman Republic's governance, Mugillanus played a crucial role in shaping the institution of the consulate, which would become a cornerstone of the Roman state.

His legacy extends beyond his own era, as the Roman Republic's system of governance influenced the development of Western democracy. The concept of the consulate, with its system of elected officials and checks on power, has endured for centuries and continues to shape modern political systems.

Despite the passage of time, Mugillanus remains a fascinating figure in the annals of Roman history, offering insights into the complexities of late Republican politics and governance.
